title: Build the model in a photo from parts riding past on a conveyor, picking out look-alikes and parking early arrivals
instruction: Build the model shown in the photo on the card, standing on the two white marks, from the parts riding on the conveyor. Take only the parts the model needs off the belt and let every other part ride off the end. You may park parts on the grey mat. Don't hold parts back on the running belt.
context: Assemblers fed by a conveyor (team assemblers, O*NET 51-2092) often work from a picture of the finished product rather than a parts list, and the parts reach them in the order they were released upstream, mixed with parts for other stations that look nearly the same; a part they miss rides out of reach. Here the only description of the model is a photo on a card. Each extra part on the belt differs from a model part in one feature, so the photo has to be read for shape, colour and height: a square post beside the round ones, an orange beam beside the yellow, a blue cube beside the red, a short cylinder beside the tall. The cube and the beam also arrive before the cylinders they rest on, so they must be taken off and parked until the cylinders stand. Each placement depends on earlier ones, so the order of work has to be planned around the order of arrival.
setup: Dual-arm station: arm bases at (0, +/-0.305, 0.75) m facing +x (x forward, y left, z up, origin midway between the bases); table top z = 0.7475 m, table 1.10 m deep by 1.30 m wide (y = -0.65 to +0.65). Conveyor: a dark rubber flat belt 100 mm wide, its running surface 25 mm above the table, centre line x = 0.35 m, running from y = +1.85 m (it comes in 1.20 m past the left edge of the table, on two 60 x 60 mm steel legs at y = 0.95 and 1.80 m) to y = -0.72 m (70 mm past the right edge); two 10 x 18 mm steel frame strips run along its sides below the running surface. The surface moves toward -y (left to right as the robot sees it) at 40 mm/s throughout the trial and never stops. Downstream tote, open, blue-grey, 10 mm walls 160 mm tall, inside 240 (x) by 200 (y) mm, its floor 0.35 m below the table top, on a steel stand beside the table, centred (0.35, -0.78) m under the end of the belt: parts that ride off the end fall into it. Photo card: a white board 240 mm wide (along y) and 180 mm tall, 4 mm thick, centred (0.534, 0.05, 0.8135) m, leaning back 45 degrees beyond the belt with its picture facing the arms and its lower edge on the table about 0.47 m forward; printed edge to edge with photo.png (640 x 480), a photo of the finished model on the white marks taken from in front of it, 25 degrees down: the two tall green cylinders standing on the marks, the yellow beam across their tops and the red cube on the middle of the beam. Fixed on the table: two white square marks 44 x 44 mm (0.5 mm thick) centred (0.20, +0.11) and (0.20, -0.01) m, 120 mm apart; a grey staging mat 160 (x) by 220 (y) mm, 1 mm thick, centred (0.20, 0.32) m. Eight loose rigid parts of painted hardwood (about 0.6 g/cm3, friction 1.2 static / 1.0 dynamic) ride on the belt's centre line, upright and square to it, at these y positions when the trial starts, in this order from the downstream end: red cube 40 mm, 40 g, y = 0.35 m; green square post 40 x 40 mm, 80 mm tall, 77 g, y = 0.55 m; yellow beam 180 x 40 x 30 mm lying flat with its 180 mm length along the belt, 130 g, y = 0.75 m; orange beam of the same size, 130 g, y = 0.95 m; blue cube 40 mm, 40 g, y = 1.15 m; tall green cylinder 40 mm across, 80 mm tall, 60 g, standing, y = 1.35 m; short green cylinder 40 mm across, 50 mm tall, 38 g, standing, y = 1.55 m; tall green cylinder as before, y = 1.75 m. Untouched, the parts reach the end of the belt 26.8, 31.8, 36.8, 41.8, 46.8, 51.8, 56.8 and 61.8 s after the start. Exact values are in layout.py.
scoring: The model parts are the two tall green cylinders, the yellow beam and the red cube; the extra parts are the green square post, the orange beam, the blue cube and the short green cylinder, which never count as model parts wherever they stand. Gate first: holding a part back on the running belt jams the line, and the trial scores 0 from then on. A part is held back when it rests on the belt (its lowest point within 5 mm of the surface) for 3 s in a row and goes less than 30 mm downstream in that time; the belt carries a free part 120 mm in 3 s, so this means stopping it for about 2.25 s or more. Knocking a part over on the belt does not by itself count as holding it back. Otherwise, at the end of the trial: 0.2 for each tall green cylinder in place, standing (its axis within 5 degrees of vertical, either end up), its lowest point within 4 mm of the mark's top and its centre within 10 mm of a mark's centre, one per mark, either cylinder on either mark; 0.3 for the yellow beam in place, only when both cylinders are: lying flat (its 30 mm axis within 5 degrees of vertical), its length within 10 degrees of the line through the marks either way round, its lowest point within 4 mm of the lower cylinder top, and its centre within 15 mm horizontally of the midpoint between the cylinders; 0.3 for the red cube in place, only when the beam is: a face down (an edge within 5 degrees of vertical), its lowest point within 4 mm of the beam's top, and its centre within 10 mm horizontally of the beam's centre. Each counted part must be at rest (under 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s). Then 0.25 is taken off for each extra part that has not ridden off the downstream end (its centre past the table's right edge and at least 50 mm below the table top, as in the tote), never below 0. Success, which ends the trial, is the four model parts in place, all four extra parts gone downstream and no jam, held for 1 s. In simulation every test uses each part's centre, orientation and true extent (box corners, cylinder rims). On a real rig: a top and a side photo with a tape measure for the model, the tote's contents for the extra parts, and the video for any part held back on the belt.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. With the belt stopped, stand the eight parts back on the belt at their starting positions in order, empty the tote, then start the belt at 40 mm/s and start the trial. In simulation the belt is already running during the 0.5 s settle after a reset, so the parts are spawned 20 mm upstream of the stated positions; run with -E device=cpu -E object_jitter=0.
fidelity: PhysX at 240 Hz in the CPU pipeline (on GPU the belt's surface velocity does not carry the parts). The belt is a fixed kinematic slab whose surface moves at 40 mm/s: no rollers, stretch or slip. Rigid parts with one friction (1.2/1.0); the green cylinders are drawn round but collide as 40 mm square prisms, as convex cylinders rocked on the belt. The photo is the simulator's render of the model. The jam is a scoring rule: a held part does not stop the belt.
